audit_status: reviewed with specialist decisions retained; not legal advice, clinical certification, security certification or regulatory attestation
method: Current official source observation is recorded separately from Oblivion source observation, audit inference and the required accountable specialist decision.

sources.title: Health Information Privacy Code 2020, including Rule 3A effective 1 May 2026
sources.authority: Office of the Privacy Commissioner New Zealand
sources.official_source_observation: HIPC applies to identifiable health information handled by health agencies including supported accommodation. Amendment No 2 incorporated Rule 3A from 1 May 2026. For indirect collection after that date, reasonable steps must make the person/representative aware of collection, purpose, intended recipients, collector/holder identity and address, the particular authorising law where applicable, and access/correction rights, as soon as reasonably practicable unless an exception applies.
sources.oblivion_source_observation: The public privacy page asserts HIPC compliance but has no Rule 3A/IPP3A content or governed effective version. Repository search found no Rule 3A/IPP3A implementation symbol. Consent, export, retention, site-scope and device/location paths are mapped to the related findings.
sources.inference: The code cannot be described as implementing current indirect-collection notice merely because a generic HIPC statement exists; collection-point applicability and any exception require a data-flow and owner review.
sources.required_specialist_decision: The accountable NZ privacy officer/legal adviser must determine health-agency role, each direct/indirect collection flow, reasonable notification steps, exceptions, notice ownership and effective-date evidence.
sources.coverage_status: Reviewed—current official source separated from code observation, inference and specialist decision

sources.title: HISO 10029:2022 Health Information Security Framework
sources.authority: Health New Zealand / Health Information Standards Organisation
sources.official_source_observation: The current Health New Zealand information-governance page exposed the official static HISO 10029:2022 core PDF, which was directly retrieved and reviewed. It frames health-information security around confidentiality, integrity and availability and the Plan, Identify, Protect, Detect and Respond functions. Current supplier guidance was also retrieved; its detailed implementations are recommendations and alternative ways may satisfy requirements. Neither document alone proves Oblivion applicability, system scope or conformance, and HIPC—not HISO—governs privacy-law conclusions.
sources.oblivion_source_observation: The repository contains permissions, policies, audit records, site-access helpers, encrypted fields and two domain outbox pairs, but the retained findings show inconsistent site/direct-object enforcement, public consent evidence, TLS disablement, and incomplete signal replay/recovery. This audit did not perform penetration testing or certify HISO conformance.
sources.inference: Individual controls do not prove an organization-wide security framework; the mapped gaps are product/code risks against the control frame, not a regulatory attestation.
sources.required_specialist_decision: The security/privacy owners must establish applicability, risk appetite, system boundary, evidence owners and an independent HISO-aligned assurance plan.
sources.coverage_status: Reviewed—current official core and supplier documents directly retrieved; applicability/conformance reserved to accountable owners

sources.title: HL7 FHIR New Zealand Base Implementation Guide 3.1.0
sources.official_source_observation: The current NZ Base IG 3.1.0 is an R4/R4B reusable set of NZ extensions, identifiers, terminology, naming systems and profiles. It explicitly does not define complete conformance for a particular implementation or use case.
sources.oblivion_source_observation: A case-insensitive search of app, routes, tests, resources/js and database found no FHIR, fhir.org.nz, NZ Base IG or nhi-id implementation reference. NHI is stored as an Oblivion field, but no FHIR endpoint/conformance surface was discovered.
sources.inference: No current FHIR conformance claim can be made, and the NZ Base IG alone would not define a future API contract. Absence is recorded as an integration evidence gap rather than a defect where FHIR is not an authorised product requirement.
sources.required_specialist_decision: Before any future FHIR surface, the clinical information architect/privacy/security owners must define the use case, authoritative master direction, implementation guide/profile set, identifiers, terminology, consent, versioning, conflict and failure handling.
sources.coverage_status: Reviewed—current official source separated from code observation, inference and specialist decision

sources.title: Ngā Paerewa Health and Disability Services Standard NZS 8134:2021
sources.official_source_observation: NZS 8134:2021 has been in effect since 28 February 2022. The Ministry describes person- and whānau-centred, outcome-focused requirements and a modular certification framework in which providers are audited against relevant sections and criteria.
sources.oblivion_source_observation: Several H&S, clinical and compliance pages render green Certified or Cover OK states without an authoritative certificate/coverage source. A shared snapshot explicitly acknowledges the missing sources and returns true; some local pages hardcode the label or use drills/FENZ status as a proxy.
sources.inference: A drill, procedure, default boolean or missing KPI cannot establish a provider/site's modular certificate status or first-aid cover. The UI claim is unsupported; this audit does not decide whether a particular service is legally required to hold certification.
sources.required_specialist_decision: The certification/clinical/H&S owners must confirm applicability, provider and site scope, relevant modules, certificate evidence, expiry/revocation semantics and operational readiness measures.
sources.coverage_status: Reviewed—current official source separated from code observation, inference and specialist decision

sources.title: Code of Health and Disability Services Consumers' Rights
sources.authority: Health and Disability Commissioner New Zealand
sources.official_source_observation: The Code includes rights to effective communication and information, presumes competence, requires informed choice/consent subject to stated exceptions, preserves choice to refuse or withdraw consent, and sets complaint handling/progress obligations.
sources.oblivion_source_observation: Consent request materialisation can convert informational next-of-kin responses into active consent and infer incapacity/best-interests decisions. Medication, care-plan, respite and clinical findings identify separate authority, relationship and amendment gaps.
sources.inference: A database status or relationship label is not itself valid informed consent, capacity evidence or authority. The code findings are safety/governance gaps, not legal conclusions about an individual decision.
sources.required_specialist_decision: Clinical governance/legal owners must approve decision-specific authority, capacity, information, withdrawal, representative and complaint semantics and validate them with representative users.
sources.coverage_status: Reviewed—current official source separated from code observation, inference and specialist decision

sources.title: WorkSafe guidance: what events need to be notified
sources.official_source_observation: WorkSafe guidance requires prompt regulator notification of specified work-related deaths, notifiable injuries/illnesses and notifiable incidents, with site preservation and records. Work-relatedness and the specified serious-event criteria are part of the decision.
sources.oblivion_source_observation: The application has notifiable flags, pending/acknowledged states and WorkSafe actions, but the classifier covers death, hospitalisation and a generic critical shortcut rather than the full specified injury/illness, dangerous-incident and work-relatedness decision tree; closure and site-scope findings affect the surrounding workflow.
sources.inference: The classifier is preliminary decision support and cannot be treated as a complete statutory determination. Whether a real event is notifiable requires accountable H&S/legal assessment.
sources.required_specialist_decision: The qualified H&S/legal owner must approve versioned criteria, uncertainty/escalation, work-relatedness, regulator choice, site preservation, evidence and sign-off.
sources.coverage_status: Reviewed—current official source separated from code observation, inference and specialist decision
